look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · American black nightshade is an UNARMED, green herb with simple alternate ovate leaves and VERY SMALL white five-lobed star flowers, often in compact clusters. On mature plants, inspect the SMALL (~5–10 mm) SHINY PURPLE-BLACK BERRIES and the tiny green CALYX LOBES bent sharply BACK from the base of each ripe berry. Check SHORT, plump yellow anthers (~0.7–1.5 mm) with a hand lens or macro photo. Crucially: multiple black nightshade species look like this from a distance—green fruit or white petals alone cannot prove S. americanum.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Solanaceae / Solanum: alternate simple leaves, fused five-lobed star/rotate corollas, 5 poricidal anthers and berry fruits. Do not assume every Solanum is prickly; American black nightshade is unarmed.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: unarmed green annual to short-lived perennial, erect to spreading up to about 1.5 m

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ALTERNATE simple ovate/elliptic leaves, typically 2–10.5 × 1–4.5 cm, smooth to slightly wavy or shallowly toothed

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: usually 3–10 tiny white flowers borne together on simple, often umbrella-like stalk groups

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: white five-lobed corolla, typically only 4–8 mm across (occasional larger variation)

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: five SHORT yellow anthers, about 0.7–1.5 mm long

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: green pea-size developing berries turning GLOSSY purple-black, approximately 5–10 mm wide

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mature fruit calyx lobes tiny and STRONGLY REFLEXED (pointing backwards away from berry)

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mature berry pedicels often ERECT or SPREADING, with the berry separating and leaving its stalk attached to plant

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Green unarmed herb, annual to short-lived perennial, from small weed to loose branching plant about 0.3–1.5 m. Can be hairless to sparsely hairy; purple tint on stems is variable, not diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Leaf
key_traits.text: Simple ALTERNATE petiolate leaves, generally ovate/elliptic with pointed tip and base narrowing toward petiole; entire, shallowly wavy or sinuate-toothed edges; FNA typically 2–10.5 cm long and 1–4.5 cm wide. Leaf margins vary, so leaf alone cannot resolve the Morelloid group.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: The tiny white five-pointed star-shaped COROLLA is about 4–8 mm wide (Flora of North America). Anthers are five, bright yellow, short and fairly plump, only approximately 0.7–1.5 mm long, dehiscing through small apical pores that elongate to slits. Flowers in small unbranched 3–10-flowered clusters, often arranged like a little umbrella from one short inflorescence axis. White flower alone not sufficient because other black-nightshade relatives are also white-flowered.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Initially green berries mature to shiny purple-black, about 5–10 mm wide, held on erect to spreading fruit stalks (pedicels). Under mature fruit the small green CALYX LOBES are strongly REFLEXED—point backwards/away from the berry instead of hugging it. Fruiting berries often detach while pedicels remain; internal seed/stone-cell counts may be needed for truly close look-alikes.

key_traits.label: Habitat
key_traits.text: Common in disturbed ground, gardens, shady margins, trails, damp or enriched soil. S. americanum is reported in Texas; exact Hays County nativity scoring remains a separate paused lane.

lookalikes.differences: The hardest look-alikes are OTHER unarmed black-berried Solanum species, particularly S. emulans and S. nigrescens, not the large prickly yellow-fruited species. Distinguish with anther length, fruit gloss, reflexed versus appressed fruit calyx, and pedicel behavior.
